question.text: Merchants from this empire and the later Songhai Empire partook in the trans-Saharan trade. This empire's ruler Mansa Musa disrupted the Egyptian economy by handing out gold during his trip to Mecca.
question.clue: That founder defeated the Sosso monarch Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.

swap.leadin: This country's emperor, Menelik II, stopped an Italian invasion of his country at the Battle of Adwa.
swap.text: Along with Liberia, what nation in the Horn of Africa led from Addis Ababa is considered to be the only African nation not to be colonized?
swap.clue: One king of this modern-day nation signed the Treaty of Wuchale.

question.leadin: This country shares Lake Turkana with Ethiopia and the Kibera slum is in its capital city of Nairobi. --.
question.text: Name this East African country north of Tanzania.
question.clue: This nation's Deputy President William Ruto avoided a July 2017 assassination attempt while the murder of Christopher Msando sparked controversy before this country's 2017 presidential election.

swap.leadin: This empire was once ruled by Tunka Manin, and its demise brought the rise of the Sosso people.
swap.text: Name this empire which had its capital at Koumbi-Saleh and gives its name to a modern day country with capital at Accra.
swap.clue: This empire was the first in its region to treat all gold nuggets larger than dust as its king's property.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Songhai Empire.
question.text: One of the Songhai Empire's most important cities was this settlement on the Niger River. This major trading hub was the site of Sankore University and the Djinguereber [Jin-gay-reb-er] mosque.
question.clue: The Frenchman Rene Caillie was the first European to return alive from visiting this city.

swap.leadin: One leader of this country used the Ruvuma Development Association as an example of his policy of ujamaa.
swap.text: Name this country, which resulted from the joining of Tanganyika and Zanzibar. Since 1974, this country's official capital has been Dodoma, though many government functions are still based in Dar es Salaam.
swap.clue: This modern-day country was the location of a war in which a British fleet defeated Sultan Khaled ibn Barghash in 38 minutes.

question.text: This West African country, with its capital at Dakar, was formerly part of the Mali federation, before splitting off to form its own country. It completely surrounds The Gambia.
question.clue: This country's capital lies on the Cape Verde Peninsula near the westernmost point of continental Africa and is home to Leopold Sedar Senghor Airport.

swap.leadin: This war included two invasions of a neighboring country's Shaba province.
swap.text: Name this lengthy war in which the communist MPLA defeated its rival UNITA.
swap.clue: Allegations that an election during this war was rigged caused the 1992 Halloween Massacre, which killed many Bakongo and Ovimbundu people.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Britain's Cape Colony in South Africa per part.
question.text: As prime minister of Cape Colony from 1890 to 1896, this founder of De Beers conquered northern South Africa and present-day Zambia and Zimbabwe.
question.clue: Charles Rudd and this man convinced King Lobengula to hand over the resource-rich Matebeland; this was known as the "Rudd Concession."

swap.text: At the 1827 death of his mother Nandi, he banned agriculture and the drinking of milk from his kingdom, leading to the coup which caused his death.
swap.clue: Mfecane resulted when the tribes nearby attempted to escape this man's forces, and he was assassinated by his brother Dingane.

question.text: Longtime Ivorian president Felix Houphouet-Boigny ["oo-foo-EH bwahn-YEE"] moved the capital to Yamoussoukro from this city, which remains the most populous in Cote d'Ivoire.
question.clue: This was the capital of Cote d'Ivoire from 1933 to 1983, succeeding Bingerville in that role, and remains by far its largest city, with over three million residents.

swap.leadin: European imperialism in Africa faced resistance from many local powers, such as the Zulu Kingdom.
swap.text: Name this leader of the Zulu during the Zulu War. This ruler consolidated rival tribes to grow Zulu borders and also introduced the "bull horn" army formation.
swap.clue: This rival of Zwide has been credited with introducing widespread use of a short stabbing spear called the iklwa, which was an improvement on the assegai.

question.leadin: This work ends with a prophecy of the eventual supremacy of its home country over Rome.
question.text: Name this Ge'ez [GHEE-ezz] text that details the travels of Queen Makeda of Sheba to Jerusalem and how the Ark of the Covenant came to Ethiopia.
question.clue: The Solomonids' descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba is chronicled in this book, whose title means "Glory of the Kings." Its 32nd chapter relates the birth of Menelik I, the son of Solomon and the queen.

swap.text: This anti-communist led UNITA during Angola's civil war. His death led to the end of the conflict.
swap.clue: This man praised the Heritage Foundation for its role in repealing the Clark Amendment.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about cities in the Middle East that saw major protests in 2011.
question.text: This city, the third most populous in Libya, was threatened with a massacre when the United States and other countries intervened militarily.
question.clue: Much of the fighting in Libya has centered on this third most populous city, which is located 130 miles east of Tripoli. It was the city that Muammar Qaddafi's forces were destroying when NATO intervened and where two American photojournalists were killed by mortars.

swap.text: This man served as the first democratically elected president of the Republic of Congo for ten weeks until he was deposed and assassinated.
swap.clue: Soon after concluding independence talks with King Baudouin ("bow-DWAHN"), this leader was forced to take refuge in Stanleyville when he was dismissed by Joseph Kasa-Vubu.

question.leadin: This man was a member of the Krahn tribe, and resentment toward Americo-Liberians fed his rise to power.
question.text: Identify this dictator of Liberia from 1980-90 who established the People's Redemption Council. He was overthrown by rebels including Prince Johnson, who flmed his torture and may have eaten his ear.

swap.leadin: Most historians believe that this empire was founded by the Zaghawa people, who gained political control because they possessed horses and ironworking technology.
swap.text: Name this empire centered around Lake Chad, the first in sub-Saharan Africa to acquire firearms. Ibn Furtu chronicled the military exploits of one of this empire's greatest mais, Idris Alooma.
swap.clue: One important mai or king of this nation named Hummay converted it to Islam and founded the Sayfawa dynasty.

question.leadin: This location was described Gilles Perrault's Our Friend the King and Tahar Ben Jalloun's bracing novel, This Blinding Absence of Light.
question.text: Name this secret prison in the Atlas Mountains, considered by many as the quintessential symbol of repression by Morocco's regime.

swap.text: Under Amin's term many peoples were massacred, including this ethnic group, a subgroup of the Luo peoples. Famous Ugandans of this ethnicity include Okot p'Bitek and the leader of the Lord's Resistance Army, Josef Kony.
swap.clue: This Luo-speaking ethnic group in South Sudan and northern Uganda, who form the core of the Lord's Resistance Army. The only Ugandan president of this ethnic group, Tito Okello Lutwa, was deposed by Yoweri Museveni ("YAH-wair-ee MUH-seh-veh-nee").
